column7: recover-admin (server/admin/recover_admin_logic.go), the one documented emergency-recovery mechanism for a locked-out admin, cleared the target account's password hash to "" with nothing to replace it. bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword (internal/core/auth.go's VerifyPasswordCredentials) fails unconditionally against an empty hash for every password, so the recovered account could never actually log back in through any documented path -- the one official recovery mechanism was itself a permanent self-DoS on admin access. Found live (design-b2-recover-admin.md's own §3 already claimed "the very first thing the recovered admin can do is log in, set a password" -- never actually true). Fixed by setting a server-generated one-time password (core.GenerateInitialCredential, the same generator CreateUserWithOneTimePassword already uses for new-user onboarding, ADR-028 Part E, hashed at core.PasswordHashCost) instead of an empty hash, printed once for the operator to relay, while keeping password_reset_required so every OTHER endpoint stays refused until a real password is chosen. Red-before/green-after proving test drives the full documented sequence through the real internal/core login/change-password code (not a re-implementation of it): recover-admin -> log in with the printed OTP -> forced password change -> log in with the new password -> confirm the superseded OTP no longer works.
